message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Step | What Happens | Key Points | |------|--------------|------------| | **1. Setup** | • Shuffle the Uno deck (108 cards).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face down as the draw pile.
• Turn over the top card to start the discard pile; if it’s a special card, follow its effect immediately. | • Each player keeps their hand hidden from others. | | **2. Turn Order** | • Play proceeds clockwise (or counterclockwise if a reverse card is played).
• The first player is the one to the left of the dealer. | • The direction can change with a Reverse card. | | **3. Playing a Card** | • On your turn, you may play one card that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top discard.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile.
• If the drawn card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | • You can only play one card per turn unless you use a Wild Draw Four (see below). | | **4. Special Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and misses a turn.
• **Wild** – Player chooses the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – Player chooses the new color and next player draws four cards and misses a turn. | • Wild Draw Four can only be played if you have no other playable card (otherwise you risk being challenged). | | **5. Winning a Turn** | • When you play your last card, shout “UNO!” before your next turn starts.
• If you forget, the next player can call “UNO” on you. If you’re caught, you must draw two penalty cards. | • Failure to say “UNO” when you have one card left results in a penalty. | | **6. Ending the Game** | • A round ends when a player discards all their cards.
• Score points based on the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Draw Two/Reverse/Skip = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50.
• First player to reach 500 points wins the match (you can set a different target). | • Keep a running score sheet; the game can be played in multiple rounds. | --- ### Quick Tips * **Keep track of the current color** – Even if you’re not playing, knowing the active color helps you plan which cards to hold. * **Use Wilds strategically** – Save them for when you need to change the color to something you have many cards of. * **Watch for “UNO” calls** – If someone forgets, you can challenge them and force them to draw two cards. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
